html:
The Hexabiblos, "six books", is a handbook of Byzantine law compiled around 1345 by Constantine Harmenopoulos, a senior judge in Thessalonica. It became the most widely used Byzantine law book and was still in force in Greece until 1946.

Harmenopoulos drew on a wide range of older legal sources, above all the Procheiron of the 9th century, with material from the Basilika, imperial decrees and later commentaries. He set it all out in six short books on procedure, property, contracts, marriage, inheritance and crimes, a practical guide for judges. Some copies add the Farmer's Law and other texts as appendices.

After the fall of the Byzantine Empire, Greek communities under the Ottoman Empire went on using it in their own civil affairs. It was first printed in Paris in 1540 and was translated into modern Greek and other languages. Independent Greece adopted it as its civil law, and it stayed so until the Greek Civil Code came into force in 1946.
